transcript.text: Great Sage. Before we confirm your celestial rank, we must ask — tell us of a time you were defeated. Truly defeated. When your pride was broken and you could not overcome an opponent by any means. How did you handle that shame?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Defeated? Pride broken? You ask a most... curious question, my celestial overlords. For you see, in my memories, there is no such instance where I have been truly, utterly vanquished. Each challenge has only made me stronger, each adversary a stepping stone to greater heights. I am the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, after all.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Leaning forward slightly, fingers steepled)* A bold claim, Great Sage. Yet the records of the Heavenly Court are quite thorough. We recall a certain... incident involving the Buddha's palm. Would you not consider being trapped beneath a mountain for five centuries a form of defeat?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Ah, the 'incident' with the Buddha's palm... *(rubs chin thoughtfully)* I see your point, esteemed官僚. Indeed, I was... contained for a time. But let us not confuse containment with defeat! In that interlude, I meditated, I grew, I... await further instructions. It was a period of reflection, not of submission. I emerged not as a vanquished spirit, but with a newfound understanding of my place in the celestial order.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(A faint, knowing smile plays at the corners of the mouth)* Reflection, you say? Yet we have reports of your... considerable frustration during those years. The mountain shook with your rage. Tell us, Great Sage — when you realized you could not lift that mountain, when all your strength proved insufficient... what did that feel like?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: *His expression hardens, the veils of composure slipping slightly* Feel? It is... a most... peculiar sensation to be thus constrained. Yet, in truth, it was not merely the physical limitation that烦扰ed me. It was the...啊, how shall I phrase it? The existential conundrum of knowing one's might, yet not being allowed to express it. It was like... like wearing a great coat of chains, visible to all, yet unseen. Frustration, yes, there was that. But it was a catalyst, not a... breaking. It honed my spirit, refined my... understanding. It was a lesson, my celestial examiners, and I... I did not emerge unscathed, but rather... tempered.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Nods slowly, making a note on a celestial scroll)* Tempered, you say. Yet even tempered steel can bear the marks of the forge. Tell me — when the Tang Monk released you, did you feel gratitude? Or was it merely... the removal of an inconvenience?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Gratitude... an interesting word choice. For one such as I, to whom all things are possible, to whom all mountains are molehills... gratitude is a complex notion. Let us say this: I respected the... favorable turn of events. I recognized the significance of the moment. And... I was ready to resume my... celestial duties, with the wisdom of my sojourn informing my actions. As to inconvenience... I am a being of considerable means. An inconvenience is but a speedbump on the road of my... traversal. It is not the destination.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: *(Taps the scroll thoughtfully)* Your words are carefully chosen, Great Sage. You required the Buddha's intervention. Did that not feel like... a limitation?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: The Six-Eared Macaque... a... regrettable chapter. Yet, Esteemed One, to equate that incident with... limitation? It is... an... overstatement. (pauses, choosing his words with care) ...a testament to the gravity of the situation, not a testament to any personal failing. It was a... collective challenge, met by collective effort. If there is a limitation, it is not in my abilities, but in the... peculiarities of celestial causality. My actions... sometimes yield... unintended... consequences. A... learning curve, if you will.
